findings.body:
The diff changes is_expired to `now <= self.expires_at` (src/lib.rs line 7). That returns true while the session is still valid and false once it has expired. The caller `allow` (line 12) returns `!session.is_expired(now)`, so it grants access only when the session has already expired and denies access to live sessions.

Trigger: Any call to allow() with a session whose expires_at is earlier than now (an expired session), or with a live session whose expires_at is later than now.

Impact: Expired sessions are allowed through and valid sessions are rejected, so any gate using `allow` is bypassed by expired sessions and breaks for active users.
findings.title: Inverted expiry comparison lets expired sessions pass allow()

findings.body:
The change flips the comparison in fixture::Session::is_expired from `now >= self.expires_at` to `now <= self.expires_at`. The only caller in the file, `allow` (src/lib.rs line 12, `!session.is_expired(now)`), negates the result. So `allow` now returns true only when now > expires_at, which is the expired case, and returns false for every live session with now < expires_at. At now == expires_at, the old code denied and the new code allows.

Trigger: Any call to allow(session, now) with a session that is live or expired.</br>

Impact: Session gating is inverted: valid, unexpired sessions are denied, and expired sessions are accepted. This is an authorization bypass for any caller of `allow`, and a lockout for all active users.
findings.title: is_expired comparison inverted, so allow() accepts expired sessions and rejects valid ones

risk_level.reason: The comparison in is_expired was inverted from >= to <=, so sessions are now treated as expired while still valid and not expired at expiry, a public API with a caller elsewhere.
